summary.headline: Standalone H1 FY27 revenue rose 26.1% to INR 64.92 crore and PAT 69.5% to INR 5.55 crore, while consolidated PAT fell to INR 1.37 crore.
summary.overview: Standalone performance was strong in Q2 and H1 FY27, driven by new verticals such as eTDR, with standalone EBITDA margin up to 35.1% in Q2. Consolidated results lagged because of a deferred Dubai/MEA order (about INR 1 crore reversed in the quarter) and higher go-to-market spend in Germany. Management highlighted a INR 92.95 crore JNPA order, an order book of about INR 300 crore and a INR 625 crore sales pipeline, and said a Middle East permitting contract is near signing. Depreciation and amortisation rose sharply, weighing on consolidated PAT.

segments.name: eTDR (TDR exchange)
segments.commentary: Platform live for about four months; charges 0.5% fee on transaction value, with revenue booked directly. Management said it drove the standalone EBITDA margin improvement, but Mumbai TDR volumes were lower in Q1 and Q2 versus last year.

segments.name: Recurring / SaaS revenue
segments.commentary: Recurring revenue INR 28.21 crore in H1 (+46.2%), 43.5% of sales; SaaS/transaction revenue INR 18 crore (+32.7%).

segments.name: International (Germany, Middle East)
segments.commentary: Germany investment is weighing on consolidated other expenses and go-to-market spend. A Dubai/MEA order of about INR 1.7-1.8 crore was deferred, with about INR 1 crore reversed in Q2.

guidance_outlook: Management sees no downside to FY27 guidance; the Dubai deferral is about 1% of top line and expected to reverse as the situation improves.
Targets booking about INR 55 crore from the INR 300 crore order book in FY27.
Expects about INR 100-125 crore of order-book revenue to be delivered in the next 12 months.
Expects to convert about 40% of the INR 625 crore pipeline, with 50-75% of that delivered within 12 months.
Expects D&A to stay at similar absolute levels, with the percentage of sales declining as revenue scales; management estimated roughly INR 25-30 crore for the year on H1 run rate.
capex_capacity: Ongoing product development for overseas markets (German alignment), TDR platform and CivitPLAN/Civit applications, expected to deliver results this year or next, driving higher amortisation.
Management said the platform and business-model transition has development costs to be amortised and depreciated subsequently.
Hired a sales director in Germany to expand business development.
demand_pricing: Order book of about INR 300 crore; sales pipeline of INR 625 crore across CivitCITY, CivitPORT and CivitINDUSTRY and other initiatives.
JNPA order of INR 92.95 crore for an AI-powered digital twin of port operations, described as first of its kind in India.
Middle East government permitting contract described as at a very advanced stage, with signing expected soon; the Dubai order deferred due to geopolitical conditions.

Mumbai TDR volumes were lower in Q1 and Q2 due to a slow real estate market and fewer permits; management said October saw better results and some more cities are expected to be added in the coming quarters.
Management said it is working with multiple cities on eTDR and has seen traction in other states, without naming them.

qa_highlights.question: What explains the gap between standalone and consolidated revenue growth, and how much is due to the deferred MEA order?
qa_highlights.answer: Consolidated was impacted by German market investment and a Dubai order deferred due to geopolitical conditions. The order was invoiced earlier, but auditors advised deferral; about INR 1 crore was reversed in Q2.

qa_highlights.question: What are the details of the MEA order deferral and is there a cancellation risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Order size was about INR 1.7-1.8 crore with a 10-12 month execution timeline. Management said there is no current risk of cancellation and it is in touch with the client on timing.

qa_highlights.question: How does the eTDR business model work?
qa_highlights.answer: Buyers and sellers transact on the exchange via an SBI escrow account; SoftTech charges 0.5% of transaction value as facilitation fee, with a transfer fee to the authority.

qa_highlights.question: Why have Mumbai eTDR volumes fallen versus last year, and are other cities interested?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the real estate slowdown and fewer permits reduced volumes; it expects growth in coming quarters and is converting more cities, without naming them. Last year's INR 8,000 crore was the full-year volume since May start.

qa_highlights.question: Why is there a deferral in the Middle East alongside a healthy engagement, and how did the engagement come about?
qa_highlights.answer: The delay is from a private client; the new engagement is with a government, which is slow to convert. Management said the contract could be signed any time and would be announced soon.

qa_highlights.question: Will D&A stay elevated, and when will it stabilise?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said absolute costs will continue at similar or slightly higher levels, but their share of sales will fall as revenue scales.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the order book is executable in 12 months and what is the win rate?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR 100-125 crore of the INR 300 crore order book is deliverable in 12 months; FY27 booking target is about INR 55 crore; about 40% of the pipeline is high-probability, with 25% of that booked in year one.

qa_highlights.question: What is the downside to FY27 guidance if the MEA order stays deferred, and how is revenue mix across the three pillars expected to evolve?
qa_highlights.answer: Management sees no FY27 downside given standalone strength and expected Middle East win. The three pillars are interconnected; management expects 10-15 similar opportunities over three years, with JNPA as a starting point.

risks_watch: Consolidated profitability: consolidated PAT fell to INR 0.21 crore in Q2 from INR 0.33 crore, with D&A at INR 6.85 crore.
Deferred Dubai/MEA order (INR 1.7-1.8 crore) depends on geopolitical conditions; the timeline for restart is unclear.
Mumbai eTDR volumes are weak and dependent on permit issuance in a slow real estate market.
Middle East government contract signing is pending and has not yet been announced; timing and size are undisclosed.
Germany market investment is adding to other expenses, with returns not yet visible.

Inconsistency to check: the call transcript says it is dated November 4, 2026 in the cover letter but November 13, 2026 in the body; the company's H1 standalone and consolidated figures and some management estimates should be verified against filings.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on long-term opportunity (CivitCITY, ports, industrial corridors, Middle East), but cautious on near-term overseas conversion and deferred revenue, with repeated explanations of delays. Management was candid that Germany and Middle East returns have taken longer than expected.
key_quotes: So, we are very confident we will be able to, kind of address wider range of such infrastructure opportunities in the country today with the help of this success being made.
We are definitely emphasizing on establishing a sustainable business rather than moving very fast and converting them into something which may not really be sustainable.
As of now, there is no risk of cancellation of this order.

growth.why: Management sees no downside to FY27 but does not quantify revenue growth; it targets booking about INR 55 crore from the INR 300 crore order book this year, with INR 100-125 crore deliverable in 12 months, backed by a JNPA order of INR 92.95 crore and a INR 625 crore pipeline. No physical capacity additions were discussed, and the Dubai deferral and weak Mumbai eTDR volumes are headwinds.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Standalone EBITDA margin rose to 35.1% in Q2 from 29.6% on eTDR, but consolidated margin slipped to 25.3% from 26% as D&A rose to INR 6.85 crore from INR 5.65 crore and Germany spend grew.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: No physical capacity additions (plants, lines, branches) were discussed; only platform development and a Germany sales director hire.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management targets booking about INR 55 crore from the INR 300 crore order book in FY27 and expects INR 100-125 crore delivered in 12 months, backed by a INR 92.95 crore JNPA order; recurring revenue grew 46.2% to INR 28.21 crore in H1, but Mumbai eTDR volumes were weaker in Q1 and Q2.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex was not discussed as a standalone plan; only development costs for the TDR platform and overseas products, which will raise amortisation.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management sees no downside to FY27 but did not quantify or raise guidance, and the Dubai order (INR 1.7-1.8 crore) is deferred with about INR 1 crore reversed in Q2.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Consolidated PAT fell to INR 0.21 crore in Q2 from INR 0.33 crore, the Dubai deferral is about 1% of top line, and D&A is guided to INR 25-30 crore for the year.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Ongoing development for German alignment, the TDR platform and CivitPLAN/Civit applications is expected to deliver results this year or next, and more eTDR cities are expected to be added in coming quarters.

rows.label: Middle East permitting contract signing
rows.why: Described as at a very advanced stage with signing expected soon, but the client is a government and undisclosed in size and timing, and the Dubai order of INR 1.7-1.8 crore is still deferred.

rows.label: eTDR expansion to more cities
rows.why: Management is working with multiple cities and has seen traction in other states, and October saw better results, although Mumbai volumes were lower in Q1 and Q2 with a slow real estate market.

rows.label: Germany investment payback
rows.why: Germany investment is weighing on consolidated other expenses and go-to-market spend, and returns are not yet visible, with management candid that overseas returns have taken longer than expected.
